summary: Saved failed or partial studies lose their outcome and failure reason at the reader boundary, so reopening them shows only a generic history/not-running state.
fix: Render the selected study's terminal state, final outcome and recorded reason in a dedicated text status, independently of the current runtime strip. Preserve that status after service retirement and reload, and cover a failed/partial archive in the browser regression.
evidence: captureStudy retains `reason: state.terminalReason ?? state.cleanupError?.message`; StudyWorkspace.message sends `state`, `terminal`, `reason` and `finalOutcome`. However, studyClient renders `Runtime — ${message.liveState ?? 'not running'}` and the observation label only; it never displays study.state, study.finalOutcome or study.reason. A deterministic harness executing the actual studyClient script with a retired archive `{state:'stopped', terminal:true, finalOutcome:'not-demonstrated', reason:'Study wall deadline expired; history only.'}` produced runtimeText='Runtime — not running', errorText='', reasonVisibleAnywhere=false and outcomeVisibleAnywhere=false. This is controller-to-view code-path evidence, not native visual QA. D6.3 requires the partial-run reason and ended-run label to remain available with historical moments; the omission also hides asynchronous prerequisite failures once their records become stopped.
test_stub: test('reloaded failed study keeps its recorded outcome and reason visible', async () => { /* Arrange a validated saved terminal archive with finalOutcome: 'not-demonstrated' and reason: 'Study wall deadline expired; history only.'; retire the service, reopen the archive and post the resulting StudyViewMessage to the real reader client. */ await expect(page.getByText('Study wall deadline expired; history only.', { exact: true })).toBeVisible(); await expect(page.getByText(/not.demonstrated/i)).toBeVisible(); });
